heroData.title: EOR in Georgia
heroData.subtitle: Hire in Tbilisi & Batumi
heroData.description: Compliant employment in the Caucasus tech hub. Navigate 2025 work permit reforms and the unique Estonian-model tax system with our expert EOR services.

steps.title: Employment Agreement Drafting
steps.description: Create a compliant employment contract in Georgian and English. Must include position, salary (in GEL), working hours, probation period (max 6 months), and termination conditions per Georgia Labor Code.

steps.title: Work Permit Assessment (March 2026+)
steps.description: From March 1, 2026, most foreign nationals require a Special Labour Permit. Employer submits application to Ministry of Health; 30-day processing time. Exemptions for Investment Residence Permit holders.

steps.title: Revenue Service Registration
steps.description: Register the employee with the Revenue Service of Georgia for tax purposes. Obtain Personal Identification Number (PIN) for tax filings and pension contributions.

steps.title: Pension Agency Enrollment
steps.description: Mandatory pension scheme enrollment. Employee contributes 2%, employer contributes 2%, government tops up 1-2% based on salary tier (under GEL 24,000 = 2% govt; GEL 24,000-60,000 = 1%).

steps.title: Bank Account & Payroll Setup
steps.description: Establish payroll disbursement channel. Salaries paid in Georgian Lari (GEL). Major banks include TBC Bank and Bank of Georgia with swift processing.

rows.label: Income Tax (PIT)
values: Flat rate on all employment income

rows.label: Social Security
values: No social security contributions in Georgia

items.title: 2026 Work Permit Requirement
items.text: From March 1, 2026, most foreign workers will need a Special Labour Permit before employment. Non-compliance fines start at GEL 2,000 (~$740 USD) per offense. Plan ahead for Q1 2026 hires.

items.title: Estonian Tax Model Advantage
items.text: Georgia uses the 'Estonian model' - corporate profits are only taxed at 15% when distributed. Reinvested profits remain untaxed, making it attractive for growth-stage companies.

items.title: EOR Turnover Requirement
items.text: Some EOR providers in Georgia must meet a GEL 50,000 minimum annual turnover per sponsored foreigner. Established EOR partners help bypass this hurdle for new market entrants.

items.title: Remote Work Hub Status
items.text: Georgia's 'Remotely from Georgia' program previously allowed visa-free stays up to 365 days. With 2026 changes, remote workers may need to reassess their residency strategy.

items.title: Annual Paid Leave
items.description: Minimum 24 working days per year. Employees can begin using leave after 11 months of service. Unused leave does not generally carry over.

items.title: Unpaid Leave
items.description: Employees entitled to 15 working days unpaid leave annually, in addition to paid vacation.

items.title: Public Holidays
items.description: 15 national public holidays including Orthodox Christmas (Jan 7), Independence Day (May 26), and Tbilisoba (October).

items.title: Maternity Leave
items.description: 126 days paid leave (143 for complications/multiple births). Benefit = 100% of daily wage, capped at GEL 1,000. Mothers can transfer 57 days to partners.

faqs.question: What are typical EOR management fees in Georgia?
faqs.answer: EOR fees range from €199 to $700 per employee per month depending on provider and service scope. Budget providers like Native Teams start at $99/month; premium providers like Deel charge $599+.

faqs.question: Is probation period allowed in Georgia?
faqs.answer: Yes, maximum 6 months. During probation, either party can terminate with shorter notice. The probation terms must be explicitly stated in the written contract.

faqs.question: How quickly can we hire through an EOR?
faqs.answer: Standard onboarding takes 3-5 business days for Georgian nationals. Foreign hires may require 2-4 weeks depending on visa/permit requirements (longer from March 2026).

faqs.question: What is the minimum wage in Georgia?
faqs.answer: The statutory minimum is GEL 20/month (private) and GEL 115/month (public) - unchanged since 1999 and largely symbolic. Market wages are significantly higher; median is ~GEL 1,040.

faqs.question: Are 13th month payments required?
faqs.answer: No statutory requirement for 13th month salary in Georgia. Any bonus payments are contractual/discretionary.

steps.title: Gross Salary Calculation
steps.description: Calculate gross pay including base salary, overtime (1.25x-1.5x regular rate), and any allowances. Standard work week is 40 hours.

steps.title: Tax Withholding
steps.description: Apply flat 20% income tax on employment income. No progressive brackets - straightforward calculation.

steps.title: Pension Deductions
steps.description: Withhold 2% employee pension contribution. Calculate 2% employer contribution. From May 2025, pension data auto-integrates with Revenue Service declarations.

steps.title: Net Salary Disbursement
steps.description: Transfer net salary to employee bank accounts. Most companies pay monthly, typically by the last working day or 5th of following month.

steps.title: Tax Remittance
steps.description: Submit income tax to Revenue Service by the 15th of the following month. Pension contributions also due by the 15th (new May 2025 deadline).

items.title: May 2025 Pension Changes
items.text: From May 1, 2025, employers no longer submit separate pension declarations. Pension data auto-links to income tax declarations submitted to Revenue Service. Deadline shifts to 15th of following month.

items.title: Currency Requirement
items.text: All employment salaries for Georgian residents must be denominated and paid in Georgian Lari (GEL). USD contracts should specify GEL equivalent for statutory compliance.

items.title: Overtime Calculations
items.text: Overtime must be paid at minimum 1.25x regular rate. Weekend/holiday work typically commands 1.5x rates. Document all overtime approval to avoid disputes.

items.title: Monthly Tax Filing
items.description: 15th of the month following the salary payment. Late submissions attract penalties.

items.title: Pension Contributions
items.description: 15th of the month following salary (changed from May 2025). Auto-integrated with tax declarations.

items.title: Annual Tax Declaration
items.description: Corporate annual return due by April 1 for the previous year. Employee year-end statements by January 31.

items.title: VAT Returns
items.description: Monthly VAT returns due by the 15th for companies exceeding GEL 100,000 annual turnover.

faqs.question: Are there regional payroll tax differences?
faqs.answer: No, Georgia has uniform national tax rates. The flat 20% income tax applies equally in Tbilisi, Batumi, and all regions.

faqs.question: How is overtime calculated?
faqs.answer: Standard overtime is 1.25x regular hourly rate. Work on rest days/holidays is typically 1.5x. Maximum overtime is limited under labor code.

faqs.question: What payroll records must we keep?
faqs.answer: Maintain salary records, tax declarations, pension contribution evidence, and employment contracts for minimum 3 years per Revenue Service requirements.

faqs.question: Can we pay in foreign currency?
faqs.answer: Salaries for residents must be in GEL. You may reference USD/EUR for calculation purposes, but actual payment must convert to local currency.

items.title: Three-Pillar System
items.text: Georgia's pension scheme combines employer (2%), employee (2%), and government (1-2%) contributions into individual pension accounts managed by the Pension Agency.

items.title: May 2025 Changes
items.text: From May 1, 2025, pension declarations auto-integrate with income tax submissions. No separate pension filing required. Payment deadline moves to 15th of following month.

items.title: Government Contribution Tiers
items.text: Annual income <GEL 24K: 2% govt match. Income GEL 24K-60K: 1% match. Income >GEL 60K: no government contribution.

items.title: Exemptions
items.text: Self-employed pay 4% into own account. Individuals over 60 (men) or 55 (women) at scheme inception are exempt.

items.title: Private Health Insurance
items.description: Top benefit differentiator. No mandatory health contributions, so employer-provided coverage highly valued. Budget: GEL 100-300/month per employee for comprehensive plans.

items.title: Meal Allowances
items.description: Popular benefit. Tax treatment depends on structure. Vouchers or on-site meals common in larger companies.

items.title: Transportation Allowance
items.description: Common in Tbilisi where commute costs add up. Can be provided as cash allowance or company shuttle.

items.title: Professional Development
items.description: Training budgets, conference attendance, and certification support. Increasingly expected by IT professionals.

steps.title: Cash Benefits
steps.description: Cash allowances (meal, transport) are taxable as employment income at 20% flat rate. Include in payroll.

steps.title: Health Insurance
steps.description: Employer-paid health insurance premiums are taxable benefit to employee. Some structuring may reduce impact.

steps.title: Pension Contributions
steps.description: Mandatory 2% employer pension contribution is tax-deductible for the company. Employee portion deducted from gross.

steps.title: In-Kind Benefits
steps.description: Non-cash benefits valued at market rate and included in taxable income. Company car, housing, etc. are taxable.

steps.title: Record Keeping
steps.description: Document all benefits provided for tax audit purposes. Maintain supporting invoices and employee acknowledgments.

faqs.question: Is health insurance mandatory?
faqs.answer: No, there is no mandatory health insurance contribution system in Georgia. However, private health insurance is the most valued supplemental benefit.

faqs.question: What pension fund options are there?
faqs.answer: The Pension Agency manages the single mandatory pension scheme. Employees can choose investment portfolios (conservative, balanced, growth) within the scheme.

faqs.question: How are stock options/equity taxed?
faqs.answer: Stock options are taxed at exercise (20% on spread). Capital gains on share sales may be taxed depending on holding period and circumstances.

faqs.question: Is 13th month salary required?
faqs.answer: No statutory requirement. Any bonus payments are at employer discretion and subject to normal income tax.

heroData.title: Incorporation Georgia
heroData.subtitle: LLC via NAPR Fast-Track
heroData.description: Register your company in 1-2 days through the National Agency of Public Registry. 100% foreign ownership permitted with minimal capital requirements.

steps.title: Business Name Reservation
steps.description: Check name availability through NAPR database. Name must be unique and not conflict with existing registered entities. Reserve online or at Public Service Hall.

steps.title: Document Preparation
steps.description: Prepare: passport copies (notarized Georgian translations for foreigners), company charter (bilingual), written consent for legal address, and director appointment resolution.

steps.title: NAPR Submission
steps.description: Submit documents to National Agency of Public Registry via Public Service Hall or online portal. Standard processing: 1-2 business days. Same-day expedited available for additional fee.

steps.title: Tax Registration
steps.description: Register with Revenue Service of Georgia to obtain Tax Identification Number (TIN). Choose tax regime: standard (15% CIT on distributed profits) or Small Business Status if qualifying.

steps.title: Bank Account Opening
steps.description: Open corporate account with Georgian bank (TBC Bank, Bank of Georgia). Requires company extract, director ID, and beneficial owner documentation. Usually 3-5 business days.

steps.title: VAT Registration (if applicable)
steps.description: Mandatory VAT registration if annual turnover exceeds GEL 100,000. Voluntary registration available. Standard VAT rate is 18%.

items.title: LLC (შპს / Ltd)
items.text: Most common structure. No minimum capital. 100% foreign ownership allowed. Single director/shareholder permitted. Ideal for SMEs and tech startups.

items.title: Joint Stock Company (სს / JSC)
items.text: Required for banks, insurance, and large enterprises. Minimum capital GEL 100,000. More complex governance requirements.

items.title: Branch Office
items.text: Extension of foreign parent company. Not a separate legal entity. Subject to Georgian taxation on local income. Good for initial market testing.

items.title: Virtual Zone IT Company
items.text: Special status for IT companies exporting 100% of services. 0% CIT on profits, 5% on dividends. Must apply and qualify through specific criteria.

items.title: Directors
items.description: Minimum 1 director. No residency requirement. Foreign nationals can serve as sole director. Corporate directors not permitted.

items.title: Shareholders
items.description: Minimum 1 shareholder (individual or corporate). 100% foreign ownership allowed. No restrictions on nationality.

items.title: Registered Address
items.description: Local Georgian address required. Can use virtual office or registered agent address. Address displayed on public registry.

items.title: Share Capital
items.description: No minimum capital requirement for LLC. Can be nominal (e.g., GEL 1). Capital must be paid as stated in charter.

faqs.question: How long does LLC registration take?
faqs.answer: Standard processing is 1-2 business days via NAPR. Same-day expedited service available for additional GEL 200. Remote registration with POA takes 1-2 weeks.

faqs.question: Do I need to visit Georgia to incorporate?
faqs.answer: Not mandatory. You can grant Power of Attorney to a local agent. However, bank account opening may require in-person verification at some banks.

faqs.question: What is the annual compliance requirement?
faqs.answer: File annual registration with NAPR between Jan 1 - Apr 1 each year (GEL 50 fee). Failure results in late fees and potential dissolution.

faqs.question: Can a single person form an LLC?
faqs.answer: Yes, Georgia allows single-member LLCs where one person acts as both sole shareholder and director.

faqs.question: What are the tax benefits?
faqs.answer: Estonian model: 15% CIT only on distributed profits. Reinvested profits untaxed. Virtual Zone IT companies enjoy 0% CIT on export income.

heroData.title: Staffing Georgia
heroData.subtitle: Tbilisi Tech Talent Hub
heroData.description: Access Georgia's growing IT talent pool. Tbilisi accounts for 70% of the country's software developers with competitive salary rates.

items.title: Tbilisi
items.text: Capital city with 70% of IT job openings. Home to major tech companies (EPAM, Exadel, Ruby Labs). Strong university ecosystem producing ~2,000 IT graduates annually.

items.title: Batumi
items.text: Growing tech scene on the Black Sea coast. Emerging as a hub for remote workers and digital nomads. Lower costs than Tbilisi.

items.title: Kutaisi Free Zone
items.text: Industrial hub with manufacturing and logistics talent. Special economic zone benefits for qualifying industries.

steps.title: Requirements Definition
steps.description: Define role specifications, required skills, and salary range. Consider local market benchmarks - English proficiency commands 20-30% premium.

steps.title: Sourcing & Job Posting
steps.description: Post on Jobs.ge, HR.ge, and LinkedIn. Telegram tech communities are effective for developer roles. University career fairs for junior positions.

steps.title: Screening & Interviews
steps.description: Technical assessments common for IT roles. Average time-to-hire: 35 days for software engineers. 68% of openings are mid-senior level.

steps.title: Offer & Negotiation
steps.description: Offers typically include base salary (GEL), vacation days (24 minimum), and any benefits. Private health insurance is a key differentiator.

steps.title: Onboarding
steps.description: Employment contract required within 1 month. Register with Revenue Service and Pension Agency. Standard probation up to 6 months.

items.title: Jobs.ge
items.description: Largest local job board. Strong for all industries and experience levels. Georgian language interface.

items.title: LinkedIn
items.description: Dominant for professional and IT roles. Growing penetration especially among younger professionals and those with international exposure.

items.title: Telegram Groups
items.description: Active tech communities for developer sourcing. Channels like 'IT Jobs Georgia' have significant reach for quick hires.

items.title: University Partnerships
items.description: Tbilisi State University, Free University, and Georgian Technical University produce strong STEM graduates. Internship pipelines effective.

faqs.question: What is the typical time-to-hire in Georgia?
faqs.answer: Average 35 days for software engineers. Junior roles fill faster (2-3 weeks); senior/specialized roles may take 6-8 weeks.

faqs.question: Are fixed-term contracts common?
faqs.answer: Both fixed-term and indefinite contracts are legal. Fixed-term contracts cannot exceed 3 years including renewals. They automatically convert to indefinite if exceeded.

faqs.question: What benefits do candidates expect?
faqs.answer: Private health insurance is the top differentiator. Flexible/remote work options, professional development budgets, and performance bonuses are valued.

faqs.question: How important is English proficiency?
faqs.answer: Critical for international companies. English-fluent candidates command 20-30% salary premiums. Russian is also widely spoken as a second language.
